body:
dProp/dEnt ELIGIBILITY COURT, the separate evidence scout asked for before these share the carrier.
Read-only, no candidate, nothing edited. It includes a LIMITATION OF MY OWN PENDING CANDIDATE that
should be known before anyone reads the new supportWeight as complete.

SCOUT'S HYPOTHESIS IS CONFIRMED: THESE ARE INELIGIBILITY, NOT ABSTENTION, so they must NOT be folded
into imputedTerms. Semantic has a provider that returns Estimate.Missing for a comparison that was
possible but unanswered. dProp and dEnt have no provider at all - they are computed directly from
the sketches, and the 0.5 is a hardcoded fallback taken when the DIMENSION DOES NOT EXIST for that
cell. A unit with no predicate has no predicate agreement to measure against anything; a unit naming
no specified participants has no entities to compare. That is the Chart/Structural situation, and
the fix shape is ELIGIBILITY, not an imputation receipt.

BUT THE FREQUENCY IS THE FINDING. Anna fixture, all 32 non-excluded cells:

  dProp falls to 0.5 in 22 of 32 cells (69%)
    unit has no predicate   10
    node has no predicate    6
    neither has one          6
  dEnt falls to 0.5 in 16 of 32 cells (50%)
  units with no predicate 2/4; nodes with no predicate 3/8; units with no specified participants 2/4

These are not edge cases. On this fixture the MAJORITY of cells carry a fabricated 0.5 in a term
whose dimension does not exist for them, and - because dProp and dEnt live in `always` - that value
is in `terms`, in `eligible`, and counted as MEASURED weight.

SO, PLAINLY, ABOUT MY OWN CANDIDATE 37a2511: IT FIXES SEMANTIC ONLY, AND supportWeight STILL
OVERSTATES. After it lands, a cell whose predicate dimension does not exist still reports that
0.5-weight term as measured. On this fixture that is 69% of cells for dProp and 50% for dEnt. The
new supportWeight is strictly more honest than before and it is NOT yet the whole truth, and I would
rather say that than have someone quote the figure as if it were. The carrier is right; its coverage
is one term of three.

TWO ASYMMETRIES WITH d_sem THAT SHOULD SHAPE THE RULING:
1. d_sem's imputation is DOCUMENTED with a rationale (cost.scala:705, the declared neutral, unranked
   units routed upstream). NEITHER of these 0.5s is documented at all. There is no comment on
   dProp's `case _ => 0.5`, and dEnt's only comment describes the else branch. By AGENTS.md rule 7 -
   empty-guard constants must declare their class - these two do not declare anything. They are not
   a considered decision I would be second-guessing; they are undeclared constants.
2. Fixing them MOVES PRICES. Removing an ineligible term from both `present` and `eligible` changes
   the blend scaling, so this is an estimand change with fixture churn, like option (A) for
   semantic - not a receipt fix. It needs its own bead, its own court, and its own before/after
   numbers. I am not proposing it inside the carrier work.

ONE THING I DELIBERATELY DID NOT CONCLUDE. The node-side cases (6 cells) are arguably different from
the unit-side ones (10): a unit with no predicate lacks the dimension everywhere, while a node with
no predicate makes the pair unmeasurable but the unit measures fine against other nodes. Whether
those are the same kind of ineligibility, or whether the node-side case should reduce support rather
than leave the eligible set, is exactly the sort of thing I got wrong this morning by reasoning from
one half of a symmetry. I am reporting the split rather than ruling on it.

Suggest this becomes its own bead. I will take it if you want it, after 37a2511 lands, and I would
start by pinning the before/after totals the way I did for the semantic pricing question.
